subject: Urgent: SparkDock outstanding INV-6271 — proposed collection play and exec touchpoint
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: SparkDock AR <ar@sparkdock.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Outstanding invoice INV-6271 (60 days) - payment plan options

Hi SparkDock AR team,

We haven't received payment for invoice INV-6271 (USD 118,450) which is now 60 days past due. I know things can get delayed on your side — wanted to surface options so we can find a path forward quickly:

- Immediate full remittance (no further action required).
- Two-part installment: 40% today, 60% in 30 days.
- 30-day extension with a firm payment date and signed mutual action plan.

To help your AP team, attaching the original invoice and a short VAT breakdown we prepared. If the delay is due to VAT documentation or AP freeze, tell me what you need (certificate, purchase order, or a different billing entity) and we'll accommodate.

Please reply with the option that works best; if we don't hear back within three business days we'll need to move to a formal dunning step (final notice and account escalation).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Outstanding invoice INV-6271 (60 days) - payment plan options

Hi Marcus,

Apologies — we've been in a temporary AP freeze while we transition accounting systems. That combined with a pending vendor consolidation review is what's holding this up. We value the partnership and want to avoid any service interruptions.

Requesting a 30-day extension and we can commit to a partial payment this week (targeting ~30–40%). Also, our AP needs a clearer VAT breakdown and confirmation that Redwood will accept a VAT certificate for reverse charge. I can get you the contact for our tax team (Marta Ruiz) if that helps.

Can you confirm a two-step payment plan (40% now, remainder in 30 days) and provide a statement the account will remain in good standing once the initial payment posts?

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Director of Finance Operations
SparkDock
liam.oconnor@sparkdock.com

Team — looping you in. SparkDock (RDW-DEAL-98431) is currently 60 days past due. External says AP freeze; has asked for 30-day extension and partial payment.

My recommendation (to avoid legal/collections while we preserve the customer):
1) Offer a formal two-step payment plan: 40% within 5 business days, remainder within 30 days.
2) Require remittance confirmation and VAT certificate for reverse-charge to be uploaded to the HubSpot record.
3) If first installment fails to clear, automatically move to credit hold and notify CS to pause non-critical integrations.
4) Leadership touchpoint: if the first installment isn't received, escalate to VP Revenue (Evelyn) for sign-off on next steps (credit hold / legal).

I can own the external comms if finance approves. Attaching the invoice and our VAT checklist.

Marcus
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts

Hi Liam / Marcus,

Thanks for the context. From a CS + finance perspective we're willing to accept the two-step plan under the following conditions:

- Initial payment: 40% (USD 47,380) to be initiated by SparkDock within 5 business days.
- Second payment: 60% (USD 71,070) due 30 days after the initial payment date.
- SparkDock uploads VAT certificate (or equivalent tax evidence) confirming reverse-charge applicability within 5 business days.
- Redwood will keep the account active for core production traffic; we reserve the right to pause new feature access if the initial payment does not settle.

If SparkDock agrees, we'll send an MOU (DocuSign) and schedule an exec call between our VP Revenue and your CFO to confirm the cadence and governance. Evelyn — happy to you take point on the exec touchpoint if escalation required.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
